Gyan Chand And Others vs State Of Haryana on 5 December,
2025
Crm-M-43643-2025 -1-
 In The High Court Of Punjab & Haryana
At Chandigarh

* * **
213 Crm-M-43643-2025
 Date of Decision : 05.12.2025
Gyan Chand And Others
 ...Petitioners
 Versus
State Of Haryana
 ...Respondent

Coram: Hon'Ble Ms. Justice Aaradhna Sawhney
Present: Mr. Alisha Soni, Advocate
 for the petitioners.
 Mr. Vishal Singh, Aag, Haryana assisted by
 Asi Satish Kumar.

** **
Aaradhna Sawhney, J. (Oral)

1. This petition for grant of anticipatory bail has been filed by petitioners, co-accused in case bearing
Fir No.395 dated 28.06.2024 registered against him at Police Station Adarsh Nagar, District
Faridabad, u/s 420, 120-B Ipc.
2.

Status Report dated 13.10.2025 by way of affidavit of Mr. Jitesh Kumar, Assistant Commissioner of Police, Ballabgarh Zone, Faridabad, filed on behalf of respondent-State has already been placed on record.
In para 13 thereof, the factum of petitioner No.6, namely, Rakesh having joined the investigation has been admitted.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioners submit that similarly situated accused have already been granted the concession of pre-arrest bail by the co- ordinate Bench of this Court in CRM-M-7829-2025 and CRM-M-36020-2025, vide orders dated 12.05.2025 & 21.07.2025,
respectively.
1 of 3
On a pointed query raised by this Court, as to whether the aforesaid orders have been assailed by the State, learned State counsel replied in negative.

sentences.text: 3. On 29.09.2025, following order was passed.

"1. By virtue of present petition filed under Section 482 BNSS, petitioners, who are accused in case bearing FIR No.395 dated 28.06.2024 registered under Sections 420,120-B IPC at P.S Adarsh Nagar, District Faridabad, have prayed for grant of pre-arrest bail.

2. Learned State counsel, on instructions from ASI Satish Kumar, submits that petitioner Nos.1 to 5 namely Gyan Chand, Om Prakash, Harswroop, Kehar Singh and Rajbir Singh have joined the investigation and their presence is not needed for custodial interrogation.
So far as petitioner No.6 is concerned, he did not report to the Investigating Officer.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner No.6 Rakesh Kumar could not join investigation on account of having suffered fracture in his hand.
He, therefore, prays for grant of one more opportunity to join the investigation.

Learned counsel submits that the presence of petitioner Nos.1 to 5 is not needed for custodial interrogation and thus, the concession of interim anticipatory bail granted earlier to them be confirmed.

5. Heard.
6.

Keeping in view the above submissions advanced by learned counsel for the petitioners as also the fact that petitioner Nos.1 to 5 have joined the investigation, interim bail granted vide order dated 27.08.2025 is hereby confirmed qua petitioner Nos.1 to 5 only, subject to conditions as envisaged under Section 482(2) BNSS.

They shall also join investigation as and when required in future by way of written notice for such purpose to be served by Investigating Officer of this case upon the petitioner; they will not tamper with the evidence nor will influence the witnesses and will not leave the country without prior permission of the Court.

7. Let petitioner No.6-Rakesh Kumar join the investigation on or before the next date of hearing.
8. Adjourned to 17/10/25."
2 of 3 4.

Keeping in view the fact that petitioner No.6 has joined the investigation, interim bail granted vide order dated 29.09.2025 is hereby confirmed, subject to conditions as envisaged under Section 482(2) BNSS.

Further petitioner No.6 is directed to join investigation as and when required in future by way of written notice for such purpose to be served by Investigating Officer of this case upon the petitioner; he will not tamper with the evidence nor will influence the witnesses and will not leave the country without prior permission of the Court.
5. The petition stands allowed.
